name: Shipping chokepoints
value: Hormuz ~20% of pre-war traffic; blockade on
summary: Iran says three tankers burned in Hormuz on 8 Nov; traffic about 20% of pre-war levels as US blockade continues
state: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said on 8 Nov that three tankers burned after using unauthorised routes, and the UAE National Guard rescued 22 people from a burning cargo ship in the Gulf of Oman. UKMTO counted eight confirmed attacks in the strait and three in the Gulf in the week to 8 Nov, with three vessels sunk; few mine claims are independently confirmed (The National). Traffic is about 20% of pre-war levels (Lloyd's List Intelligence via The National); Windward counted at least 16 transits in the 20 hours to 14:00 UTC on 6 Nov. US Central Command says it has redirected 147 vessels and disabled five since July (Al Jazeera).
for_you: Crews and operators in the Gulf face direct risk; UKMTO issues incident warnings for mariners. Oil, gas, fertiliser and freight costs worldwide stay exposed to the disruption.
rubric_hit: Hormuz traffic materially impeded, about 20% of pre-war levels: Alert line

sources.title: The National — 'Smoke blanketing the strait': Iran steps up campaign of threats to shipping
Al Jazeera — US launches task force to disrupt Iran's land-based supply routes

why: Around 30% of seaborne oil and much container trade passes Hormuz, Bab el-Mandeb/Suez, Panama and Malacca; disruption raises prices worldwide.
drivers: Houthi/Iran attacks, war-risk insurance, drought (Panama), naval incidents, piracy.

rubric.alert: Hormuz traffic materially impeded, or any chokepoint closed, or two or more disrupted at once.
rubric.watch: One chokepoint disrupted (attacks, large-scale diversions, draught restrictions).
